objective: Review the latest commit (HEAD) on release/0.3.1/test/windows-temp-cleanup in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-rmfix, which routes the Pi tests' temporary-folder removal through a helper that retries while Windows holds the folder.
scope: Run git -C /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-rmfix show HEAD. Cause: on the Windows CI runner, extension.test.ts failed in cleanup with EBUSY on rm of a temp folder that a child process had used as its cwd.

Check that the helper retries only on EBUSY, EPERM and ENOTEMPTY, gives up with the real error within a bounded time, keeps force semantics for a missing folder, that every former rm site now uses it with the same path, that no assertion changed, and that its tests would fail without the retry. Weigh whether rm's own maxRetries/retryDelay would be simpler in Bun (several packages/runtime/tests files already use maxRetries: 5).
constraints: Do not check out other commits in any checkout and make no edits.
Report in under 300 words; mark each finding blocking or non-blocking with file and line.

criteria.text: Cleanup retries on the Windows lock errors, is bounded, and changes no assertion
The helper's tests fail without the retry

result:
result: Merge-ready. No blockers; two non-blocking notes.

Built-in `/code-review` (medium, `5d2bed8d...aff721ae`) ran and was the built-in. Its four findings, classified:
Use rm's `maxRetries`/`retryDelay`: optional. I could only check that Bun 1.4.4 accepts the options. I could not trigger EBUSY on Linux to prove Bun's rm retries on Windows. The existing `maxRetries: 5` uses (`packages/runtime/tests/{stdin,cli,host}.test.ts`) are equally unproven. An explicit, tested helper is defensible.
Budget of about 0.9 s (10 attempts × 100 ms): optional. It is bounded, but a slow runner could outlast it. Raising `ATTEMPTS` is cheap if EBUSY recurs.
Cleanup not in `finally` at many call sites: rejected. That pattern already existed and the diff keeps it unchanged.
A cleanup error masks the real failure: rejected. Same behavior as the old `rm`, and it only happens after the retries are exhausted.

Own review:
Retry codes: `temp-folder.ts` L19-21 rethrows immediately unless the code is EBUSY, EPERM or ENOTEMPTY.
Bound: it throws the original error at attempt 10, at most about 0.9 s of sleeping.
Force semantics: `{recursive: true, force: true}` is unchanged, so a missing folder resolves.
Sites: `rg '\brm\('` under `packages/integrations/pi/tests` finds none left. The diff shows each site now calls the helper with the same path, and the `rm` imports are dropped. No assertion line changed.
Tests, run: `bun test .../temp-folder.test.ts` gave 3 pass, 0 fail.
Tests without the retry: the first test (EBUSY, EPERM, ENOTEMPTY then success, 4 calls) and the third (`calls.length > 1`) would fail. The second (EACCES, 1 call) passes either way, as intended.
Lint: `mise run lint` exited 0 ("No problems in 244 files"). I did not run the full `mise run verify` or the other tests.

Non-blocking: `temp-folder.test.ts` L33 asserts `calls < 50`, a loose bound. It would not catch `ATTEMPTS` set to 40, but it does show the retry is not unbounded.

evidence:
Cleanup retries on the Windows lock errors, is bounded, and changes no assertion: `packages/integrations/pi/tests/temp-folder.ts` L9-24 (code set, 10 attempts, throws the original error); `git show HEAD` shows no assertion lines changed and no `rm(` calls left.
The helper's tests fail without the retry: `temp-folder.test.ts` L19-22 and L33-36 need more than one call; `bun test` exit 0 with 3 pass.
findings: no blockers; non-blocking items are the 0.9 s budget (`temp-folder.ts` L6) and the unverified Bun rm retry alternative (`temp-folder.ts` L9).

acceptance.rationale: No blockers; retry codes, bound and sites checked against the commit; two non-blocking items (budget, loose test bound) go to the final repair round.
